newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA'S RESERVE MONEY SLIPS IN FEBRUARY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA'S RESERVE MONEY SLIPS IN FEBRUARY.

text.p: The daily average of Romanian reserve money, the cornerstone of this year's monetary policy, fell to 5.87 trillion lei in February from 6.9 trillion in January, central bank (BNR) data showed on Thursday.
Reserve money, also known as monetary base or high-powered money, includes cash in circulation and in vaults and banks' minimum reserves.

The decline in reserve money reflected the BNR's continued drive to mop up liquidity from the market, using monetary levers to fight rising inflation and restore confidence in the leu currency, local bankers said.
Reserve money was 7.1 trillion lei last December, when it saw a monthly rise of 12.2 percent led by seasonal factors.
Monthly inflation soared to 13.7 percent in January from 10.3 percent last December. Inflation is expected to quicken in the months ahead with fuel, power and food price hikes.
The daily average of cash in circulation dropped to 4.46 trillion lei in February from 4.94 trillion in January. It accounted for 75.9 percent of February's monetary base.
Banks' minimum reserves slipped to 1.19 trillion lei in February from January's 1.67 trillion as most banks missed targets turning short of reserves on the backdrop of a cash- starving money market.
